newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds continue to slip on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds continue to slip on profit-taking.

text.p: Argentine bonds were lower early afternoon Friday as investors took profits after the surge in prices through January.
"The profit-taking that started yesterday is continuing, compounded by a decline in U.S. Treasuries," said a trader.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.30 to 125.45 while the FRB Brady bond due 2005 fell 1/2 to 89.
"The market may fall another half point before continuing its medium-term climb," said another trader.
The first trader pointed out that since nearly all papers had touched their highs in recent weeks it was no wonder there was some profit-taking.
This week's successful placement of Argentina's $2.0 billion 20-year global bond was one of the main engines of the recent rally.
